      "observations": [
        "All 27 owned diff lines in the single production path were read. The five added lines make onLoad require the event and return unless event.target is this document. The unchanged window listener is not registered with once. This is a target filter before window.arguments, gCalendar assignment, color/control initialization, title focus and notification value setup; it is not a general deduplication flag or an assertion that repeated same-document events are impossible.",
        "The actual dialog loads the properties script with defer and uses an HTML input type=color. Its XUL label control and aria-labelledby both reference calendar-color. The existing enable/disable setup can disable that input through disable-with-calendar. No label, role, focus order or input type is changed by this landing.",
        "The unchecked initialization previously could run all its assignments for a different event target; the new early return skips them. The primary reports picker failure and duplicated notification UI and tentatively suspects DOMContentLoaded, while the source proves only the target guard and skipped initialization. Native picker document/event production and historical nightly-only enablement remain unpaired/report scope.",
        "The accepted properties-save path writes the input value to gCalendar on dialogaccept. Existing browser_calendarList editing coverage writes colorElement.value = '#009900', accepts the dialog, then checks the list's computed color/name; a second opening checks the saved input value. It never opens the native picker or triggers the reported extra load event in the inspected test segment. No new test or assertion is added.",
        "The unchanged bounded test assertions omit messages in several places; these are existing callers and not additions in the five-line patch. They are not evidence of native picker, duplicate-notification or target-guard regression coverage. No missing-should-only finding is made.",
        "The event guard is a clear early return with a blank line before the initialization block. The function's existing opening-summary comment explains window arguments but does not document the new Event input or target-filter reason. A local comment/JSDoc refinement could name the initialization boundary once the actual alternate event producer is confirmed; no global event-listener policy is inferred.",
        "Complete primary current0–3, activity/footer and full own review were read. The primary describes picker failure and duplicate notification UI, says DOMContentLoaded is probably involved and historically scopes feature enablement to nightly. These reports remain distinct from the proven event-target guard and do not establish current channel policy.",
        "The own review explicitly acknowledges that the existing test sets a color value instead of using the new picker. Actual accepted test code confirms that weaker path, while the production guard precedes all initialization. The author's Firefox-test comparison remains an unread upstream statement; no engine pairing or fresh picker/notification/a11y execution is inferred."
      ],
